questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to choose a destination in Europe in order to get the Erasmus grant. I choose Italy because I love the culture and food, and have been here at lot with my family. I wanted to go a place that felt kind of "homey", so I would quicker adapt to my new home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to get the crucial information regarding the mobility. The University could, however, have been more stringent in what mails they send out. I received A LOT of mails, which made it extremely confusing to find the necessary information. As much of the information included in the mails was irrelevant, when I only wanted information about the logistics in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the website uniplaces and found a really good apartment. The Facebook page for students were extremely helpful in getting roomies!!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the campuses are spread all over the city. Check which one you shall attend before choosing a place to live. The city might not look that big, but it can be really time consuming to get from one side to the other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I received too many emails with unnecessary information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email with credentials for their 'Absalon platform' called UNIMI and UNIMIA. I registred for the courses online and used the guidelines I had received via email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidelines send to be my email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guidelines. Read the course descriptions thoroughly before signing up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was adequate. Slightly easier than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is pretty much the same. However, there is another hierarchy between students and professors than what you're use to from UCPH. The exams are time pressuring and closed book.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Human Resources Management, Hiring and Recruitment, Conflict Management and Negotiation, Learning and Development.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conflict Management and Negotiation was really interesting! It had a level of psychology, and the professor was really motivating and created an inspiring learning environment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Italian foods are really inexpensive. Some foods common in Denmark were not as cheap or available. Eating out wasn't very expensive. Coffee is really cheap!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't think the city was as interesting as I hoped. Within the first month I had seen all there was to see. The culture, however, is wonderful to experience. The food, the people, the clubs. Just walking around in the city is really nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any organised activities by Erasmus og the university. Clubs, restaurants, and shopping were really good though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Eat out. A lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bologna, Como.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it that hard. There is of course differences, but overall fine to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask them about recommendations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The hierarchy between students and professors was probably my biggest cultural challenge. Also their education system is quite different. The level and quality is not that high, and for exams you must memorise everything. This was really challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the weather.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The teachers levels of English may vary, you need to be proactive if you want information regarding exams, lectures etc., the exams are very different from the Danish exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was really helpful to have a network of other Danish students. And roomies, wouldn't have been without that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting international friends - it really is an amazing experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Handling the exam forms, as the exams are time pressuring and closed book.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
